question: bachelor party spot, loud, handles large groups
answer: For a lively bachelor party spot, Pat O'Brien’s is a great choice. The place is bustling with energy, especially with large groups, and the dueling pianos add to the fun. However, be prepared for a noisy environment. Acme Oyster House is another excellent option, especially if you're looking for a place that handles large groups well. The food is delicious, and the service is friendly, making it a perfect spot for a bachelor party.
contexts:
[Pat O'Brien’s] Pretty cool bar just off of bourbon street.  They have a few different rooms such as their main bar (which was dead), the back patio (which was bumping with drunkards soaking up the sun), and your dimly lit piano bar which had two ladies bumping requested tunes.  

Do order their Hurricane here.  It will knock your socks off.
Don't order anything else besides that or beer.  I ordered an old-fashioned (wtf was I thinking?) and the bartender threw some crap together that reminded me of college.  He even used his bare hands to rip the orange meat off an orange slice just for the peel.  I just hoped he washed his hands ...

Anyways, the dueling pianos was a blast.  The crowd was mixed, including your bachelorette party, older seniors slamming down a few hurricanes, drunk frat boys pounding beers, and your standard 30's people like my wife and I.  However, everyone was having a super fun time which was awesome.

Bathrooms are really dingy but what do you expect?

4 stars!

[Pat O'Brien’s] I don't get the big deal with this place.

It seems only really fun if you're already really drunk. Don't ever start here.  And don't expect any dancing except for the drunken sway. 

great place to stand around and talk and people-watch, I guess? 

We went in with a group of girls for a bachelorette in coordinated outfits. guys were just standing around awkwardly, holding their luke warm beers. The bar is huge and we walked through most of it but it's pretty obvious 11:30pm is not a happening time here.

[Pat O'Brien’s] We went to the courtyard to celebrate our 50th anniversary - and after stopping in the night before, we were looking forward to a nice FUN evening.  The very nice man told us just to come on down and they would take care of us.  Well, apparently our "man" was not on duty on Saturday.  We arrived at the courtyard, and the girl finally noticed we were waiting at her podium - after all she was giggling with several young fellow workers at the time.  She then seated us right outside the kitchen doors - felt the breeze of bodies going past with their trays of food.  When asked for a different spot she said that maybe in 15 minutes - sit along the side to wait.  We decided to sit inside the little bar instead - very noisy but a table nonetheless.  Charlie was our server and within minutes made us feel welcome.  The beer was served in cans, no glasses -and my Pimms cup was very good. We ordered Shrimp Jumblya and crawfish ettufie (pardon the spelling) - both dishes were very GOOD - feeling better about our choice of celebration locations. Then Charlie brought us a marvelous bread pudding dessert with two spoons - oh, my! Very good.  After we ate, we wandered to the piano bar, but soon left to find some Jazz.  Would recommend the food here - and young clueless staff aside, a good spot.  Thanks, Charlie!  You saved the evening.

[Acme Oyster House] This restaurant was great for our group of 10 who were in town for bachelor party weekend. Everyone's food was delicious and prices were reasonable. Waitress had no problem cashing us out at a timely manner and was very friendly might I add.

[Acme Oyster House] This restaurant was great for our group of 10 who were in town for bachelor party weekend. Everyone's food was delicious and prices were reasonable. Waitress had no problem cashing us out at a timely manner and was very friendly might I add.

[Jacques-Imo's Cafe] The first time I heard of this place, was years ago on TV.  Since, I had many many friends tell me that it was an experience that I had to enjoy for myself.  So... I went, and it was worth it.

A group of my friends went on a bachelor party weekend.  We ordered a disgusting amount of food, allowing us to sample everything.  I tried the fried chicken on numerous recomendations- as well as the red fish.  Both were fantastic.  

The atmosphere, the service, and the food all combined for a great experience.

[Jacques-Imo's Cafe] We came as a group of 11 girls in town for a bachlorette party last Saturday night. I was very very pleased.

We arrived early for our reservation, it is about a 15 min cab ride from Canal St..  As I went to get a round of drinks from the bar the hostess found me and told me our table was already ready.
The tablecloths are a mixmash of colorful oilcloths and are festive, the murals on the walls are pretty and unique, personal touches everywhere!
Our servers were great.  The food prices were a little higher than expected but everything is large enough to share. 

Everyone was really happy with the items we tried- 
Watermelon Mojito- Fresh watermelon and mint, light, refreshing, YUM!
Cornbread muffins- garlicky & buttery goodness
Alligator Cheesecake- most were reluctant to try but I thought it was great! A quiche consistancy with a great cream sauce.
BBQ Shrimp (beware, they still have their heads if that kind of thing ookes you out) but the buttery, garlicky, rice underneth is heavenly.
Fried Roast Beef Poboy- Was massive! 
Fried Chicken- Heard audible "yummmms" from that end of the table, two of them splitting it couldn't even finish off the plate.
My favorite side was the corn (apologies it does have a fancier name.)

Chef Jack came and welcomed us then later sent a complimentary round of champagne for the bride. Call me a dork, I love this kind of personal service.

We were loud but fit right in and from beginnng to end everyone left with a smile on their face. We went nextdoor to the Maple Leaf to join our new found restaurant friends and a good time was had by all.

[Jacques-Imo's Cafe] Stopped by for dinner on a Friday night during my bachelor party with a party of 8. Reservations must be made in advance for parties of 5 or more...that is something to keep in mind.

Sat down immediately after getting some free shots from Jacques himself at the bar. Hostess and waitress were both great and made our meal experience all the better. The restaurant itself has a very cool funky, New Orleans feel to it. It is also right next door to The Maple Leaf...so if you have to head across town for dinner you can add to your long trip by grabbing a drink and possibly catching some music next door afterwards.

Onto the food. Appetizers included the Shrimp Alligator Sausage Cheesecake and Gumbo. Cheesecake was very good and worth ordering based on its uniqueness alone. Gumbo was solid, but nothing you can't have anywhere in town. We also had these awesome garlic corn muffins with green onions...fantastic little things that will leave you asking for more.

I ordered the Redfish as an entree and I wasn't disappointed. Perfectly blackened with a nice sauce...great fish and dinner! I also tried the shrimp etouffee which was just so-so (as shrimp etouffee goes, I love the version at Acme Oyster House).

Overall, nothing blew me away...but I'd love to go back to this restaurant on another occasion to see if something else will! Really enjoyed everything...food, atmosphere, and staff made me a fan who will come back on his next trip to New Orleans.

[Ruby Slipper - New Orleans] My bachelorette brunch was absolutely amazing! The food was delicious and worth every penny. Our waitress was very fun and made great recommendations. We had a pretty big party but everything flowed smoothly and our food came out within a reasonable time. The French Toast Batons tasted like heaven on a plate! Whenever I'm back in New Orleans, this will be a definite stop. The only recommendation I'd make is to use the online reservation app to reserve a spot before you arrive. Through the app, our wait was 45 minutes and we were able to walk in once we arrived.

[Ruby Slipper - New Orleans] This is a fun place. They do a clapping routine for people's birthdays which is way less embarrassing than singing and gets everyone in the restaurant involved. Food is very good. Can't beat the boozy coffee and eggs Benedict menu. Great service and great atmosphere.

[Ruby Slipper - New Orleans] On Friday 24th of May, 2019 we started hubby's birthday celebration on our trip in New Orleans, Louisiana with Brunch at The Ruby Slipper, which he chose. This place is very popular so make sure you join the wait list before strolling through the streets to this establishment, which we did. Hubby ordered The Trifecta- 3 different style Eggs Benedict. One serving each of the Egg Conchon (apple braised pulled pork), Chicken St. Charles (fried chicken) and Shrimp Boogaloo (creole style tomato sauce) Benedict. They were served on freshly baked Buttermilk Biscuits. The eggs were perfectly poached and Aaron loved the entire dish. I ordered the Hot Smoked Salmon Omelette with Goats cheese, topped with dill, hollandaise, red onion and flash fried capers. My meal was absolutely delicious and I will say the small piece of Buttermilk biscuit that I tried was the best I've ever had. It was soft and not dense at all, in saying that I'm not a huge biscuit fan. You can order potatoes or fruit as your side with this dish too. Bloody Mary's and Mimosas are very popular over here when enjoying a Brunch. I order the Ruby Slipper Big Easy Mimosa which has OJ and a dash of Pomegranate added to the champagne. I must say this is the best mimosa I've had yet since moving to the States. They were not wrong when they said easy pour mimosa either! We sat at the bar so I watched them being made. A large wine glass 3/4 full with champagne then topped with juice for $10. Hubby had the Vodka based Bacon infused Bloody Mary which also was amazing! Overall the staff were fabulous, friendly and very accommodating on a usual busy long weekend Brunch morning. The menu has lots of choices and the meals were a fantastic price. A great birthday brunch was had and my husbands iced coffee on a very warm NOLA day to go was also very good to top it off!

[The Maison] Every night we were in Frenchman we ended up being drawn in by good music in the maison. 

Thursday night was Dysfunktional Bone at like 11pm at night. I could not stop dancing.  We experienced tradition of passing the tip bucket so many times in nola but DB was my favorite because all the horns walked through and played right in front of you while they collected tips. The place was a mad house 4 rows thick with drunk dancing people but the crowds parted and the energy was palpable when they joined the crowd. One of my favorite memories of nola was when this band did a jazz remix of the "thong song" it was so much better than the original that just had good beat and hook, they totally made this song there own.

My hubs went online and paid for a table reservation at maison. It was a bit pricy almost $100 bucks for 2 entrees and 2 cocktails. The sazarac, shrimp and grits & duck were as good as the food we ate at Commanders Palace. It was one of the best dates I've been on in the 20 years I've been dating my hubs. Our waitresses name was Shelly and she was attentive, had great recommendations and took an awesome photo for me to commemorate the night. The band playing at 7pm when we checked in was "8 dice cloth." The crowd was a mix of older folks and 30 somethings like us at the start but this band really has a flavor that appeals to so many different demographics. We stayed in our seat eating drinking and captivated for almost two hours. Of all the groups we heard this was the only CD we would not leave without. We are road tripping and have listened to this CD over and over. I wish they had taken a sharpie and written there contact or where I can get more of there music because they aren't on amazon, I've already looked. 

Food: $20 bucks person good

Vibe: all ages and progressively more dancing later. At 7pm there were families with kids and millennials at the bar. 

Service: shelly is awesome-sauce 

Music: Go here!!!! Thursday Dysfunktional Bone and Friday 8 Dice Cloth.

question: cheap brunch place with outdoor seating
answer:
Café Amelie is a great option for a cheap brunch with outdoor seating. The review mentions enjoying the breakfast sandwich, the special potatoes, and the soft and crispy ciabatta, all while sipping on a mimosa. 

The Country Club, while not explicitly mentioning outdoor seating, offers bottomless mimosas for $10 on weekends, which is a big plus. The service is excellent, and the atmosphere is fun, making it a great choice for a casual brunch.
contexts: [Café Amelie] Weekend brunch outside on the patio is a must! The food is delicious and the atmosphere is so classy! I got the breakfast sandwich and it was affordable and filling. The potatoes were special and not your average bland roasted potatoes. The ciabatta is soft and crispy. Enjoyed every bite with my mimosa

[The Country Club] We had the pleasure of dining in at The Country Club for Sunday breakfast. We made reservations in advance (highly recommend doing the same) and were seated at our table in no time. Heather took wonderful care of us and we did not once see the bottom of our mimosa glasses!!! She even took us to the pool after we ate to check it out. We're so thankful of her service and how amazing everything was. Definitely the highlight of our food we had over the weekend!

[The Country Club] $10 bottomless mimosas on the weekends!!!! That is really all you need to know!!

Food = Yummy. I especially enjoy the fried green tomato benedict. 
Mimosas = Flowing. definitely more champagne than OJ in that mixture. You take one sip and they refill your glass, now that's what I call service! 
Atmosphere = Fun. Everyone is here to have a good time. Make a reservation, it gets super crowded. 
Service = See Mimosas. Excellent.

I have never been to the pool, always too full after brunch. Maybe one day....! Separate review to come once I do.

[The Country Club] This place is in a beautiful building in a nice quiet area of the bywater. The people that work here are so fun and personable. My favorite time to be here is Sunday morning at the bar with bottomless mimosas. The food is always on point.

[Russell's Marina Grill] I've never been here before. Met friends for lunch. A bit of a wait but if you're fine with sitting on the patio, there is no wait. Bottomless mimosas and bloody marys were a plus , not to mention the great food and service.

[Trenasse] Imagine being exhausted after running a half marathon and just wanting to relax...then you hear unlimited mimosas for $10...SOLD!!!

Went to this lovely establishment after a race with a group of friends.  The hostess seated us promptly and the waitress was very witty and friendly.  The majority of our group had the bottomoless mimosas.  The waitress kept the champagne and orange juice flowing.  AFter about an hour, our group was feeling very nice....I had a lovely bluecrab omelet with potatoes and nice french bread.  Would definitely go back...:)

[French Toast] Made reservations through OpenTable. Arrived and it was busy weekend so we were seated at bar (party of two). Mimosas for drinks and cool part is we could see through the receiving window and watch our food cooked. Energy was upbeat and food was delicious

question: jazz brunch with live music
answer:
Atchafalaya Restaurant offers a fantastic jazz brunch with live music, though the noise level can be a bit distracting. The food is top-notch, with standout dishes like the fried green tomatoes and shrimp and grits. 

Buffa's Bar & Restaurant is a great choice for jazz brunch, with a lively female-led band and a packed room that still manages to be enjoyable. The food is basic but done well, and the $5 bloody Marys are a perfect complement. 

Tableau provides an excellent live jazz experience at brunch, with a bottomless mimosa bar and delicious food. The live band comes to your table, adding a unique touch to the dining experience.
contexts:
[Atchafalaya Restaurant] Brunch. Fried green tomatoes with lump crab meat. Shrimp and grits. Bloody Mary bar. Live jazz music. 
Great food. My fried green tomatoes were lick the plate worthy. If I hadn't been on a first date, I probably would've. Just kidding. Not really. He had shrimp and grits, yummm! Live music was too loud to carry on conversation. Awkward.
Nice place though if you're already deaf.

[Atchafalaya Restaurant] Super cool ambiance for brunch with live jazz. Great service and really liked the vibe of the place. The food was good, but didn't blow me away. I got the chicken and biscuits, which was nothing special. The build your own bloody bar is a nice touch.

[Atchafalaya Restaurant] Great brunch experience with the parents.
Live jazz music downstairs. Was great music but made it too loud to sit in the front room, so be sure to ask to be seated in the upstairs room.

Eggs Atchafalaya and Eggs Louisianne are both great. Grits and Grillades qerw great too, with surprisingly large chunks of meat (just a bit too much black pepper added at the end to the meat though).

Great service. Excellent bloody mary bar. (but the bm mix seemed a bit thin).

I will definitely be back!

[Buffa's Bar & Restaurant] Love this neighborhood spot for its jazz brunch. The female-led band knows their stuff. Each music set is lively and fun. The brunch menu offers basic breakfast dishes, which are done well. I had eggs, hashbrowns, bacon and grits --  all good. The eggs Benedict with homefries was good as well. And $5 bloody Marys are the perfect complement to the meal and ambiance.

[Buffa's Bar & Restaurant] Come to jazz brunch with at least 2 hours- it's packed, but the music and atmosphere is worth it!

This Sunday morning, there were 2 super women serving this back room with red walls and a little stage. These women hostesses, bartended, and served a room of 50+ guests. I hope Buffa's owner considers giving these lovely women a break, and giving customers a chance to eat in less than 2 hours.

The food is very cheap, and very okay. For $9, i had a tasty homemade biscuit with 2 poached eggs and hash browns. The hash browns serving was very crispy and very small. Coffee is solid and only $1.5.

The music was excellent. An 8 piece jazz band that has such a lovely flair. 

Pro tip: come in after 1pm. The band was still playing and the place is much less crowded.

[Buffa's Bar & Restaurant] My favorite place
Jazz brunch was the tits and so
Was the food and drinks

[Tableau] One of the best meals we had in New Orleans. Brunch on Saturday included live jazz going from table to table. Food was excellent, seafood gumbo served with baguette was great, followed by amazing and fresh main courses, nothing overcooked or under-spiced--tasty. Fun cocktails as well as mimosas to choose from. Had to ask for water and lemon twice, but other than that, they were very friendly. I would go here again and would recommend it.
[Tableau] Jazz brunch was a treat! Bottomless mimosas table side band that plays tunes by request with delicious food! What more could a New Orleans gal ask for??!

[Tableau] Can't leave without trying out Tableau for brunch. Live band coming around the table is an extra touch. Drinks were the highlight. #hellohelloeats #eattheworld #foodporn #musteat #livetoeat #eatswithlovedones #withmybb#icjourneys #eatwithcin #flexitarian #ourchoice #NOLA

[Live Oak Cafe] Live Oak has become my favorite brunch place Uptown.  The huevos rancheros are what keep me coming back, but I am a big fan of their creamy, cheesy grits too.  I also appreciate that they accommodate those on a vegetarian diet by subbing avocado for meat in their dishes.  Their coffee, from French Truck, is top notch too.  The staff all seem to be hardworking, fun people who check on the customers regularly, especially to make sure said coffee is refilled.  Grant waited on us the last time and made us laugh.  And of course there's the live music, which is an added bonus at brunch.

question: late-night Cajun food after a show on Frenchmen Street
answer:
Atchafalaya Restaurant is a top choice for late-night Cajun food, especially if you're looking for a unique dining experience. The chicken andouille gumbo and pasta atchafalaya are highly recommended, though be prepared for a slightly higher price point. 

Buffa's Bar & Restaurant offers authentic Cajun food at a reasonable price and has a 24-hour kitchen, making it perfect for late-night dining. The live music and friendly atmosphere add to the experience, though some might find the place a bit small. 

Jack Rose is another excellent option, known for its amazing Cajun food and beautiful atmosphere. The duck and sausage andouille gumbo and the mile high pie are standout dishes, and the service is exceptional.
contexts: [Atchafalaya Restaurant] Yelp directed me to this as one of the best cajun places open late on a Sunday night. Good call yelp. Live music, darkly lit, very cool restaurant. The chicken andouille gumbo and pasta atchafalaya were pretty awesome. Loses one star for being a bit too snobby with the wine. Not a glass for under $11. But otherwise great place.

[Atchafalaya Restaurant] This was the first meal I had in New Orleans during my weekend trip and it set the tone perfectly for the food adventures to come. I've always loved New Orleans style cooking but damn, the people here just blow my mind. Don't think I'll ever eat Cajun anywhere else again. 

Came for brunch. Parking sucks, but that's not unique to Atchafalaya. We ordered: grapefruit Bellini, shrimp and grits, chicken & biscuits, duck hash, and the étouffée omelet. We had "an hour" wait but was more like 20 mins. 

Everything was delicious, but things could've been better. Duck hash barely had duck, the étouffée omelet fell a little flat in flavor, the chicken and biscuits were divine (biscuits are the PERFECT amount of sweetness and fluff), and the shrimp and grits were above average, though I've had better. I would say omelet and chicken and biscuits were the better two dishes, but over all still an amazing meal!

Qualms: the price is a little steep compared to some nearby places, and the place is a little tiny. If you're cool with that then this would probably be the perfect place to come for a bougier but unarguably delicious meal.

[Atchafalaya Restaurant] This restaurant was my introduction to Cajun/Creole food and it rocked my world. I loved the shrimp and grits and the fried green tomatoes. It's a charming little place a couple of blocks from Magazine street; the ambiance was just lovely, the hostess/restaurant owner was incredibly friendly and helpful and the amazing food just kept coming.

[Buffa's Bar & Restaurant] This gets 5 out of 5 for the following reasons:
-Authentic cajun food at a reasonable price matched with reasonable quality
-Authentic New Orleans establishment that has been around for many many years
-Staff & owner are awesome human beings
-Live music in the back room!
-24hr kitchen!
-Two different bars, depending on your mood. The corner entrance is a smokey dive that allows dogs and you can still order from the kitchen. The back room (not 24hrs) is sit down dining, smoke free, and often has good, local live entertainment

When friends visit I will always take them to buffa's. There may be better "fine dining" in NOLA and arguable better cajun food, but the mix of decent food, amazing new orleans atmosphere and 24hr service makes this place a must.

[BB King's Blues Club] You must come here for food and amazing live music. We tried the chicken fried chicken - delicious, fresh, and cheesy. The sautéed veggies were so tasty we got an extra side order.  We also had the debris fries - the roast beef was so tender the gravy delicious, I added a bit of hot sauce and bbq sauce and it was amazing. We also had the skillet shrimp - the garlic bread was delicious and the shrimp were so tender. The drinks were tasty - the hurricane was delicious and the Long Island was strong. We finished off the night with a brownie sundae which was just what we needed to end a great night.  It was a bit dry but it tasted home made I still really enjoyed it. The showstopper was the B.B. king band they were hilarious and kept our feet tapping and hands clapping the whole time. We went in for dinner and stayed for like 3.5 hours we had a great time.  I almost forgot the service - Rodie was amazing!!! The best server we have had although all our servers in New Orleans have been amazing. She was outstanding I can't say enough good things about her service and menu knowledge.

[Jack Rose] There is a reason why there is a fully booked night at Jack Rose. You can't go wrong with amazing Cajun food and a beautifully decorated atmosphere. To go down the line of what we ordered on a Friday night, I'll break it down from apps to desserts. 
Fried Calamari is a shareable, seasoned, crispy appetizer  paired with a delectable remoulade. The fried chicken Parmesan was the right amount of crispiness. The chicken wings are served with a side of linguine pasta. The bowl of duck and sausage andouille gumbo was incredibly flavorful. The cocktails are crafted with imagination and not to mention, a generous amount of alcohol. The mile high pie is a Neapolitan dessert to die for! Most importantly, the waiting service and manager are very much accommodating. All the good eats on their menu is definitely worth every penny! Don't forget to take a snapshot in front of the Lil Wayne painting. It makes good for your Instagram!
Up the elevators is a connected bar, Hot Tin which has a bird's eye view of the upbeat city of New Orleans. There is no denying this is the go to spot for any occasion. So like the locals say, "Laissez les bons temps rouler!"

[The Original Pierre Maspero's] The original Pierre Maspero's is a great location to sampled some of New Orleans Cajun cuisine in the Big Easy.

It has large doors that open onto the tourist filled streets of the French Quaters. It is in an older building like much of the downtown area, with brick walls and gaslighting. There is an older handcrafted wooden staircase next to the bar which leads to the second floor, it is unique and shows how the structures were constructed in the olden days. 

Check in using your Yelp app and you will likely get a free appetizer with the order of two entrees.

We try the BBQ shrimp appetizer shrimp served in a Buttery Cajun sauce and some bread. It was very tasty. This was a 13 or $14 appetizer which was free after checking in to Yelp. What a deal!

The blacken jambalaya was excellent and hit the spot. It was not too spicy, seasoned just right. The BLT chicken sandwich had a different spice on it... perhaps rosemary and was not as tasty as the blackened chicken.

Overall this is a great place To enjoy lunch or dinner in the French Quarters, relax your feet and enjoy the sites.

For a beer selection we tried Abita the boot which was light crisp and tasty. The large size is 24 oz and only $2 more than the small.

[The Original Pierre Maspero's] Woot. Decently priced Cajun and Creole food in the heart of the Quarter with no wait on a Saturday night? Awesometown! 

Our server was a sweetheart. She was friendly, informed and prompt. The red beans and rice were bomb! My bf had chicken parmesan and it was southern fried chicken parmesan with angel hair pasta and so tasty!

Will definitely return here. If you can get a window seat, ask for one so you can watch all the people walking by. =)

[The Original Pierre Maspero's] We just stumbled upon really good Cajun food and cocktails in the heart of the French quarter! We ordered Cajun blackened chicken with fettuccine Alfredo and blackened shrimp jambalaya! I had the perfect storm cocktail and my husband had the hurricane. Shelly was our waitress and she was a hoot and really quick to get you what we needed even though it was a packed house!

question: family-friendly seafood place with parking
answer: Bon Ton Cafe is a great family-friendly option with an amazing focus on seafood, making it a perfect choice for a meal out. Mr Ed's Oyster Bar - Bienville offers a cozy and delicious experience with tasty seafood beignets and shrimp po'boys. Deanie's Seafood, while popular and often busy, is a must-visit for its incredible fried seafood platters and generous portions, though it can be a bit touristy.
contexts: [Bon Ton Cafe] Great family restaurant tucked in the quarter. Limited menu with an amazing focus on seafood done well!  Highly recommended.

[Mr Ed's Oyster Bar - Bienville] Cozy little place with friendly service. I had the seafood beignets and they came with a tasty remolaude to dip in and hubby had the shrimp poboy. They were both delicious!

[Orleans Grapevine Wine Bar & Bistro] Cozy little restaurant just off of bourbon st. They offer a great selection of wine, cheese, and elevated dishes. We had some wine, a cheese board and the steak tip appetizer. The wine was great, and the cheese board was very good. The cheeses were uncommon but palatable for everyone. They even had a chocolate cheese that tasted like fudge, we saved that for last. The steak was ok but I wasn't overly impressed by it. The cheese board was so good we stopped in a few nights later and got it again to go. The service was great both times. Great place.

[Le Bayou Restaurant] Seafood restaurant on Bourbon St.  Fast friendly service. This was a spur of the moment choice, the alcohol and tireless walking had set it. The restaurant was packed, but we were sat rather quickly.

Chicken and Sausage gumbo- it had a very nice texture to the soup- not too watery and not too thick like gravy. The pepper overtones kind of took over the dish, but overall quite satisfying. 

Oysters, bacon bits, and cheese. - was a bit of disappointment. On the dry side. Hardly any bacon on the oysters. C-minus at best. 

Overall it's a Good place or a quick bite.

[Deanie's Seafood] Does this place really need another review? Oh what the hell, I'll give the 1001st!
I'm gonna make this simple. It's in the Quarter. There will be tourists. It's a family restaurant. There will be children.  It's a popular place. There will likely be a wait, but it's a big place and you can wait indoors. It's mostly seafood, with few other choices. Everything I have ever ordered here has been ridiculous. The service has been accommodating.  I don't have one single complaint for Deanies.  I don't care that is full of tourists and children, it's convenient when I visit and I get my craving for fried stuffed shrimp satisfied here

[Deanie's Seafood] After searching the Quarter for good, reasonably priced meals for 20 years now I think we found a gem in Deanie's Seafood! Restaurant was hopping on a Wednesday night (good sign)-20 minute wait for table. I think I had the BEST crawfish etoufee ever-and I can make a good one. Dining partner's gumbo was also really tasty--nice, thick roux--puts Acme's & Felix's to shame.  Those cute little (spicy!) (free) potatoes they serve as an "appetizer" are good, too! We didn't try the oysters but heard they get theirs from the same supplier as Acme & Felix's so they're probably great, too.Fried seafood platters were HUGE!!  Nice big bar--packed with people. Looked like mostly locals---as they've been in business in Bucktown for a long time.  Walked away fat and happy and still had $$ in our pockets--not bad!

[Deanie's Seafood] My FAV seafood (FRIED PLATTER-wise) in the French Quarter area. This place is spacious and full of southern hospitality. The wait is usually up there for a table (nothing like those long drawn out waits at Acme) unless you time it correctly.

The staff are true Nawlins and I LOVE IT from the Southern twang to the way they celebrate life like there is no tomorrow. 

We almost always get the same items
- Crab Nachos
- BBQ Shrimp
- 1/2 seafood platter 

The potatoes that come out before the food is amazing. I warn you "Don't eat too many as you won't be able to finish your meal if you do". The potatoes are so fresh and tasty with the butter.
Crab nachos are good but pretty much a heart attack on a platter due to all be cheese and such added. I tend to only take a bite or so to say I had it. The BBQ shrimp is extremely messy you must prepare to get messy. The 1/2 seafood platter is the HIGHLIGHT of Deanies (most people get the whole but I don't suggest this unless you are with a group of 4 or more). This platter screams flavor filled with various seafoods and tasty treats l like shrimp, scallops, fish, hush puppies, corn, etc..

A must do every visit to NawLins ;-)

question: quiet romantic date spot
answer: Langlois is a fantastic choice for a quiet romantic date night. The reviews highlight its excellent wine pairings and the interactive dining experience, making it a memorable evening. Chappy's Restaurant offers a charming ambiance with its outdoor patio feel, perfect for a date night. However, be aware that it might be a bit noisy, as one review mentions the lively atmosphere. For a quieter option, 9 Roses Cafe is highly recommended for its perfect warm pho, making it a great spot for a quiet and cozy date.
contexts: [Langlois] Fantastic and fun evening.  Excellent wine pairings.  Go!  You will not be disappointed.

[Langlois] This was the best date night we've ever had...we did the cooking competition on a Saturday night and the moment we walked in we felt super comfortable yet so excited! We made so many new friends, got to learn a lot of really game changing cooking tips from Chef Mel, and for $60/person - we were full off of amazing food! (first glass of wine is free too)! We will definitely be going back.

[Langlois] We returned to Langlois for another fabulous date night!   Interactive dining at its best!    We have been here several times and each visit is better than the last.   The staff is attentive and courteous, anticipating our needs but not intrusive at all.   We are almost on a first name basis with everyone there!   Each time we visit,  our participation in the food preparation is different and we are always pleasantly surprised with how much we learn.   We love that the menu is seasonal and,  being a farmer's daughter,  the farm to table menu suits me perfectly.   Very inexpensive for a five or six course dinner (I lost count) along with wine pairings and bubbly!   Thanks, Chef Amy and Chef Tess, for a delightful time!  We'll be back!

[Chappy's Restaurant] Cute restaurant tucked at the end of magazine.  You walk in and you feel like you're sitting at an outdoor patio underneath the stars.  Entrees come with choice of salad or soup with a side.  Great price.  Had the spiced shrimp that came with jambalaya and a crab cake on top.  Delicious and perfectly spiced.  Service was impeccable and attentive.  Perfect date night spot.

[Jamila's Mediterranean Tunisian Cuisine] Such a wonderful experience! The food, service and atmosphere were delightful. We got the shrimp and mussels tarragon pasta, salade tunisienne and couscous royale. All of them were delicious, but the personal service is what made this place so special. Great date night! Can't wait to go back

[Jamila's Mediterranean Tunisian Cuisine] The ambiance and service (including the jovial owner and his son) provided the perfect date night environment! Delicious food too! Definitely going back soon!
[The Tasting Room] Great casual gathering place with great wine and food . Group of friends or first date it's the perfect spot . Mark

[The Tasting Room] Love the newly renovated location. The management and bar are all super welcoming. 
We didn't try food but we did try the $6 chambongs. Definitely worth the price. The patio area is really cool..even though the weather is super moody. 
I would highly recommend here for a date night, gurls bight, bachelorette weekend and any other event involving twirls and a good time!!
[The Tasting Room] This place is awesome. The food is great and the staffs knowledge of wine was impressive. Very nice for a date night. Definitely try the crab cakes.
[9 Roses Cafe] Perfect warm pho on a cold night. Great find off the main path if you're looking for a quiet spot.

question: outdoor patio restaurant with a full bar
answer: Mid-City Yacht Club offers a spacious and comfortable outdoor patio with a fountain, fans, and misters, making it a great spot for a drink and some food. The Bulldog Mid City has a chill outdoor patio that's perfect for a relaxed evening, with plenty of seating and a variety of games to enjoy. The Rusty Nail's outdoor patio is one of the nicest in town, spacious and clean with plenty of fans, making it a great place to enjoy a drink on a hot summer night.
contexts:
[Mid-City Yacht Club] The atmosphere is not like a traditional bar !
The outside patio is very spacious and has a fountain. To keep the patio guest cool there're many fans and misters making things very conferrable
The foods offered are full of different variety.
We stopped to have drinks and a bite with friends while on vacation . this first visit was a great experience  and we will be back .

[Mid-City Yacht Club] Been here over a dozen times, I love the vibe and the staff. Inside is always fun and lively, whereas the back patio is a bit more toned down and relaxing. You can sit outside under the lights and just hang out or go inside and get a little loud. They have pool, darts, and some egambling as well. Love this bar and love its location!

[Mid-City Yacht Club] Cool LOCALS bar with awesome AC inside in addition to an outdoor patio. 

16 taps and plenty more choices in the bottle and can. 

We got Yachtchos (nachos) as snack. Fresh made chips and habanero crema really hit the spot.

[The Bulldog Mid City] I have been coming here often for years. Love this bar! It is always fun with a date or with a group of friends. The seating area in the back outdoor patio is nice on a cool night. They have a large selection of beers on tap. The food and the service is top-notch as well. I suggest going for their trivia night. It's always a good time.

[The Bulldog Mid City] When I think of bars, I can't help but think of loud music and obnoxious people. Why can't there be a bar that's chill with space to move, music that's fun and not too loud so you can actually have a conversation? Oh wait! That's The Bulldog Mid City! 
I completely enjoyed the outdoor patio even in the drizzling rain. Gabe and I went here after our dinner at Luke at his suggestion. He was a regular here awhile back and always talked about how I might like it. I loved it! Great old school music and such a variety too. The crowd was in the 30-something range.... late 30's and older maybe. 
What I usually hate about bars is how cramped and stuffy they can be. The outdoor patio gives us claustrophobs a place to not freak out while looking for a stool near the exit. 
The canopy of trees with lanterns and string of lights are a nice touch. Definitely look forward to going back.   
I couldn't think of a reason not to give it 5 stars. 
Great music, beer, atmosphere and company!

[The Bulldog Mid City] Visited the Bulldog Mid-city twice in the last year. I really like the patio mostly because it is DOG FRIENDLY. No waitress service for food or drinks. If it's crowded expect to wait at the bar for drinks and sometimes the kitchen gets overwhelmed and closes when they get behind. WAY TOO LOUD INSIDE TO HAVE PLEASANT CONVERSATION. 

Once you get situated the patio is very nice. TVs around to watch the game and the draft beer selection is great. I agree with other reviewers that the beer is overpriced especially considering the smaller sized pitchers used which contain about four beers. The nachos were reasonably priced and very good. We'll be back........

DOG FRIENDLY ON THE PATIO.

[The Rusty Nail] Perfect neighborhood bar.

Good selection of liquor.

They've been steadily improving the outdoor patio area, which is fantastic on a nice-weather evening/afternoon.

[The Rusty Nail] All around great bar.

The staff is always friendly and attentive. The outdoor patio has a great ambience. And Tuesday night trivia is always a blast.

[The Rusty Nail] Great downtown bar that straddles the line between dive and classy joint. Recently changed to no smoking indoors, but that's okay because their patio area is one of the nicest in town - spacious, clean and plenty of fans for those hot summer nights. Bar serves strong and affordable beverages from a nice selection by friendly bartenders. Plus, the talented Jen "Motha F*in" Howard may mix a drink or sing a song for you, depending on the day. They still have the Mermaid Lounge sign up in the back of the patio, giving homage to its predecessor. Tip: there is a parking lot reserved for Nail patrons that you can get to behind the bar, off of Calliope. Dog friendly and they have food though I haven't tried it yet. Their support of various nonprofits through guest bartender nights is just the cherry on top!

[Feelings Marigny Cafe, Bar & Courtyard Lounge] This place is a hidden gem! Came here for an early dinner. Since the weather was nice, we decided to sit outside. The courtyard is really cute! In the evening, once it got dark, they had lights around the trees. The patio chairs weren't that comfortable to eat a meal, more for lounging with a drink...but they had some really quaint patio furniture (I had my eye on a hanging round chair).
However, we found out that they don't serve their full menu in the outside patio bar, so we had to order from the appetizer menu. Not that's a big deal because everything on the appetizer menu still looked good. I also ordered a sazerac, and good, albeit  bit strong for my taste. For food, we ordered the oysters, garlic shrimp, ribs, pommes dauphine, and the jumbo lump crab.   Everything was really delicious! Incredibly flavorful and bold.
[Twelve Mile Limit] Small bar - great atmosphere and great bartenders. Always a friendly crowd. The outdoor patio has a cozy vibe!

question: dog-friendly restaurant with a patio
answer:
Barracuda is a great option for a dog-friendly outdoor dining experience, though the weather can be a factor. The back patio is cute with picnic tables, and it's very dog-friendly with multiple large dogs present during your visit. 

Satsuma Café offers an excellent choice with both indoor and outdoor seating, and it's highly dog-friendly. The place has a great vibe, especially in the Bywater area, and the food is highly recommended, particularly the breakfast options and sandwiches.
contexts: [Barracuda] You order at a window up front then sit and wait out back - outdoor dining only. The back patio area is cute with picnic tables. It's a little too cold out now for eating outside, even though they do have heat lamps. The place is very dog friendly - there were three large dogs at other tables while I was there. The menu doesn't have much variety- just a few different tacos, and I thought they were just ok, don't really have much seasoning or flavor. but there is a mushroom taco if you don't eat meat. It's a nice ambiance for warmer days.
[Satsuma Café] Real good food. Outdoor patio and dog friendly in addition to indoor seating. I like this place and will be back.

[Satsuma Café] I love this place. They have excellent breakfast options, and their sandwiches are some of the best in the city.

It's in the Bywater so it has vibe of that area, and there's outdoor seating.

They are pet friendly, people typically have their pets outside while eating.

[Trenasse] Love that this restaurant is in a dog friendly hotel and thus dog friendly by virtue. They have seating so you can sit with your pet outside of the restaurant but at the bar, just case someone doesn't want to sit beside a dog. Service is top notch and food is great and reasonably priced. I've had the Benedict's and this last time had the oyster log. Amazing price and delish. You get a total of 18 oysters. So good. I will be back!

[Trenasse] If I could give it 6 stars, I would. Reservations usually aren't needed, but on Yelp it said they allowed pets, so I made a reservation through OpenTable and noted that we have a small dog. I received a call from the host who informed me that only applied to service animals, but she offered to set up seating on the patio for us and the dog. The patio had an awning and it rained hard but was still in the 70s. We had the gumbo, the blue crab bisque, a shrimp entree and mahi mahi. For dessert it was beignets and peach cobbler. Everything was spectacular. Our server was the most attentive server I have ever had...which is especially great when you're the only party on the patio and servers sometimes forget about them. Ours was Johnny on the spot. We were on a long trip across the country and had been doing a fair bit of fast food and takeout, so it was nice to have a great dining experience.

[Chais Delachaise] I love this place! The ambience is cozy, the food is delicious, and they have a great patio. I have had the pleasure in speaking to one of the owners in my visits and she's very hospitable. One of my favorite dishes is the crab and pepper salad. It's fresh and delicious. It's a special so grab it when you can! If you just want to go for some drinks and small plates, it's a great option. If you want an artfully crafted sit-down meal? Go for it. And the patio is dog-friendly, so bring your fur-kids!

[Dat Dog] It's mostly outdoor seating, with the inside seating completely open. The outdoor seating is covered and very cute, a large area. They only had one dark beer on tap, but it is the south... so many options it was hard to choose! They even have vegan sausages! Lots of toppings including toppings made here. However, there being no description e steered clear. I had a house special, the Crawfish Etouffe Dog, because I wanted something fun and there were so many topping options. My husband had the alligator dog with bbq sauce, bacon, grilled onions and cheddar cheese. Both were delicious. We split the seasoned fries. Definitely a fun place, pricey for hot dogs, but these are specialty dogs. Seems a favorite with the young people, college and younger aged people here. If you have your dog (canine) with you or live here, this is a great place to go and bring it.

question: upscale dinner spot that takes reservations
answer: For an upscale dinner spot that takes reservations, I highly recommend Emeril's Delmonico. The review describes an amazing dining experience with VIP treatment, impeccable service, and a menu that can't go wrong. Another excellent choice is Cafe Sbisa, which offers a small but exquisite menu, a cozy atmosphere, and attentive service. Commander's Palace is also a top pick, known for its formal and elegant ambiance, excellent service, and a fine dining experience that feels fresh and intimate.
contexts:
[Emeril's Delmonico] BAM!

They say if a restaurant seats you at the window, it means they think you're attractive and want to advertise your dining experience to those walking by. I mentioned this to my group moments before they tell us our table is ready and SEAT US AT THE WINDOW.

So instantly we felt like stars, getting the VIP treatment. Okay probably... they were spoiling us as much as they do all the other patrons. But really, this was an amazing dinning experience. It is an extremely elegant restaurant, without feeling stuffy or too mature for my group to feel comfortable.

You can't go wrong with anything on the menu. But be warned, you can't do Bourbon Street after you eat here. You'll be too full, and you won't want to contaminate your tummy, now filled with Emeril's treasure, with cheap booze. So plan your night accordingly:

Make your reservation,
Arrive on time (wearing pants and shoes! They'll awkwardly tell you this when you make your reservation),
Dine like royalty for a minimum of three hours, and
Walk, rather than cab, back to your hotel, so that you can maybe build up the appetite to do this one more time on your trip. 

It really doesn't get better than Emril's in New Orleans!

[Emeril's Delmonico] Went to Delmonicos to celebrate our last night in NOLO and made reservations...of course. 4 woman who have been friends a long time to enjoy the "essence" and "flavors" of the best of NOLO. We were early for our 7pm reservation directed to the bar and was seated at a table adjacent to the bar with piano and loud "bar" patrons.
Service instant but then felt rushed to order and then we could not  hear each other asked for another table.  Resturant was not full...We were then told we could not be changed. ..We then paid for the drinks and left...with They were sorry....for a place that has a reputation of fine dining it was extremely disappointing. As patrons we were treated less than.....when making reservations make sure to book a table in dining room only!

[Cafe Sbisa] Sunday the 23rd we were a party of four
For dinner. Called for reservations and were sat immediately when we arrived . 
Our server was "Story" and she was excellent.  The atmosphere was  elegant ,antique, Orleans with candle light and white table cloths. Just what we were looking for. The menu is small which means every dish is prepared exquisitely. 
The attention to detail, flavor and ingredients was impeccable.  The service was outstanding.  If you plan to dine here, please do it arrive disrespectfully dressed.  No- jackets are not required but no floppy floppies ! This restaurant is worth your time and effort.

[Cafe Sbisa] Best experience I've had in a long time! 

Let's start with the energy of this restaurant, impeccable! I did make reservations in advance via open table and someone called me 3 hrs prior to arrival to confirm our reservations. It made it feel so personable! When booking your reservations you can state what your visit/special occasion is for. I put down that I was visiting for a date and our waiter was very attentive to our needs and provided us with amazing recommendations. 

The music was great. 
The pace of the waiter, the food, and check was perfect.

Will be returning again!

[Commander's Palace] From the time we made the reservation we felt welcomed. Found them to be courteous, professional, knowledgable, and friendly the entire experience. The ambiance is something out of the 50s, but does not feel dated. Fresh and intimate space that is what fine dining experience should be. Men are encouraged to wear a jacket and no shorts. White table cloths, candle lights and servers waiting to fulfill your every need. Formal, fancy fun. Great to make your night feel special but not at all stuffy.

[Commander's Palace] I'd never been escorted to the ladies room in my life, I kinda liked it.

I called in on Saturday afternoon for dinner reservations for the same evening. Thankfully, we were able to get a reservation for Saturday night  for dinner for 2 at 6:00 PM because they had a cancellation. 

Service is great! Awesome receiving line as you enter the restaurant. They sat us in the Garden Room, which feel like you're sitting in the tree tops. We were able to watch the sun set from up there. It was beautiful.  The staff were super attentive, polite and courteous. I had the gumbo of the day, lamb shank and bread pudding for dessert.  My sister had a side of spinach, fillet Mignon and strawberry shortcake for dessert.  Everything was delicious. 

Save some extra cash if you're going to have dinner here, it's worth it.

[Commander's Palace] If you want to experience an impeccably run establishment, look no further. From the moment we called for reservations and I gave my husband's name and they already had the rest of his information, even though I was calling from my cell phone until the moment we left and the valet had our car waiting for us by the time we got downstairs the service was flawless. 

We arrived a bit early so we had pre dinner cocktails in the courtyard. They came and got us when our table was ready. It was nice to be somewhere where people actually dressed for dinner. (You didn't have to be formal, but most men had on a jacket without a tie and most women either a dress or a nice pantsuit.)

The food was fresh and well presented. We wanted to do the seven course tasting menu with pairings, but alas we were driving. That will have to wait for another night.   We had the three course menu.   It was excellent. The highlights were the trio of soups and the bread pudding soufflé. 

Don't miss the Cafe Broulo (sp) if you've never had it. We ended our dinner with it. It was a wonderful coffee drink prepared table side, quite a show, excellent, and to quote our waiter it's supposed to be as dark as night and as sweet as sin. It's an experience not to be missed!  Try it!  You can thank me later.

[GW Fins] Impeccable service and attention to detail.  Made reservations on OT noting we were in for our anniversary.  Were attended to by excellent waitstaff all around.  A great dinner and experience.  Thank you!

[GW Fins] Tried to get a sat night reservation at 5 pm on a sat night... 10:15 availability.  So, we just delayed and made a 7|30 mon night reservation.   Found it to be a nice space right off bourbon st.  Tables not too close , classy enough, but not over the top classy.  Smoked oysters appetizer yummy.  Both of our fish dishes were vey fresh (drum and halibut) with creative , tasty sauces.    No rush, no hurry, but attentive enough staff.

Notes, I give this a 4 compared to another even better experience at surprisingly  ...  Adolpho's...   on Frenchmen street.

Note, maybe you can get lucky trying to get seats and a meal at the bar without a reservation.  That's just a matter of chance ...otw ..make fri, sat reservations early.

[GW Fins] Upscale date night alert !

Make a reservation, dress up, and enjoy a romantic dinner here. I knew what to expect, and The Fin delivers. 


This is a luxury experience convenient to the Bourbon Street shenanigans. We were able to easily walk from the room to this location. We, of course, grabbed a few drinks along the way. 

Thank you for the 5 star experience!

[Broussard's] Came here for a nice dinner with my wife. If I could give it a 3.5 stars I would. When I came here, this place had 4 stars which is why I chose it, based on the reviews from others. But I don't think it lived up to 4 stars. 

We got there fairly late on a Tuesday night around 8 or so and there were clearly open tables. The hostess asked if we had reservations, which we didn't. She explained almost secretly that they only seat people after they've made reservations, so we stepped out looked them up and made a reservation for 5 mins later on the Open Table App. It wasn't a big deal and at least the hostess was nice enough to let us in on "the secret" but I almost left for that reason.  Just seems to me that you wouldn't want to inconvenience a potential customer? I'm not going to beg you to take my money for an overpriced meal. But maybe they do this so that they get a certain type of customer, ones that are used to making reservations for nicer places to eat? I'm not sure but again seems like a bad business practice. 

So for the actual meal. The dining room was decorated very nicely and it's definitely a classy place, which is good because that's what I wanted for date night with my wife. I ordered a cocktail, Whiskey and Waterloo. It was awesome maybe my favorite cocktail yet. I was undecided, between that and another whiskey cocktail so I asked the waiter and he gave me a good recommendation.  I love crab cakes so we ordered that as an appetizer. It tasted delicious and was very nicely garnished. But it was just barely warm. I would say it felt like just above room temperature. I've worked in a restaurant so I understand that stuff happens, not everything can be piping hot right out of the pan and the wait staff only has so many hands. And at nicer places chefs/cooks don't want their food sitting under heat lamps. So I gave them the benefit of the doubt. I ordered their Pompano Ponchartrain and my wife had the Fillet Mignon. And when they brought out entrees out, the same thing again. Food was only warm. Again both tasted great. If I went back I wouldn't get the pompano again. It was good but nothing incredible. My wife said the Fillet was great, she doesn't get seafood very often so she would probably order it again. 

Overall, nice place, good wait staff, great cocktail, food tasted good but was just barely warm when served. I went with a 4-star expectation and it undelivered just slightly.

question: happy hour bar with TVs to watch sports
answer: La Carreta is a great spot for watching sports during happy hour with its fun atmosphere and yummy queso. Trenasse offers a fantastic happy hour with delicious oysters, tasty boudin balls, and amazing street tacos, making it perfect for sports watching. Pythian Market is another excellent choice, especially if you're looking for a variety of foods and drinks, with a great Harvest Moon bourbon cocktail and a lively atmosphere.
contexts: [La Carreta] Yummy queso and tequilla drinks. Fun atmosphere. Great for large groups of people or when you want to watch a little football and pig out.

[Trenasse] Happy Hour is the way to go - fresh delicious oysters, flavorful BBQ shrimp and reasonably priced drinks, Everyday!
We sat at the bar and really enjoyed watching a football game and seeing the bartenders in action.

[Trenasse] We stayed at the Intercontinental for 3 nights and came down to the hotel bar for 2 of those days.  The happy hour is from 3-6pm everyday.  The drinks generally range from around $5.  The happy hour drinks offer a pretty wide selection but if you want to try one of the higher end drinks, you'll have to pay full price.  The bartenders are generally very friendly and the atmosphere is relaxed.  There was live music on one of the evenings we were there. 

We had a half dozen chargrilled oysters for $11 and it was delicious.  I would definitely recommend giving it a try.  Overall, a nice place to stop by and have a few drinks.
[Trenasse] Boudin balls, debri fries and the smoked wings were AMAZING!! Good for happy hour and not expensive at all! They have the stink juice cocktail which was amazing! The prices are great!

[Pythian Market] This is a great place to meet up with friends for happy hour b/c there are a variety of foods and drinks.  Plenty of space and the music was jamming.  The Harvest Moon bourbon cocktail is delicious.  If you like rosemary try this.  Street tacos and pepperoni pizza were perfect for happy hour!
[Tableau] Loved everything I ate. They have a good looking burger for people who are picky. Happy hour drinks are awesome! $5 select mixed drinks and draft beers 2-5
[Tableau] Loved everything I ate. They have a good looking burger for people who are picky. Happy hour drinks are awesome! $5 select mixed drinks and draft beers 2-5
[Tableau] French 75 and pecan pie - my personal fav. Great happy hour cocktails .. The balcony view is the best view.. Very French-y

[Sala] Great food and good vibes, does it get any better than that?! Recently went here for happy hour with a friend. Service was fast and drinks were plentiful. 

We tried so many different small plates but the standouts were the duck empanadas and sweet chili fried calamari. They have an extensive drink menu to try plus a full bar if you want to sick with your regular. I  got a gin lemon drop and it did not disappoint. 

Great location with parking on the side.  An not wait to try again.

question: BYOB place with casual attire
answer: Cleo's Mediterranean Cuisine is a great BYOB option with a casual vibe. The place has a fantastic decor and a Kwik Mart nearby for picking up a bottle. Marcello's Restaurant & Wine Bar offers a unique pick-your-bottle wine policy and excellent service, though it's a bit more upscale. Lola's is another BYOB choice with a relaxed atmosphere and a great experience, though it might be a bit pricier.
contexts: [Cleo's Mediterranean Cuisine] The food here is fantastic and we enjoyed the bring your own bottle policy. There is a Kwik mart across canal st that you can go and purchase alcohol at to drink with your meal. I also loved the decor! It didn't feel like New Orleans at all inside .

[Marcello's Restaurant & Wine Bar] Our group of 13 was quickly seated despite our short notice reservation. Elliot, our server, was fantastic! She was personable and highly attentive to each of us. The pick-your-bottle of wine option was unique and the food was superb. Flavorful and distinct entrees - swordfish, linguine tritone, boar - are not to be missed. Clean and comfortable atmosphere invites you to take your time amd enjoy the company.

[Marcello's Restaurant & Wine Bar] Delicioso! We were able to pick out our own bottle of wine from their vast selection in the back of the restaurant. Amanda was great! Highly suggest. We will be back

[Marcello's Restaurant & Wine Bar] This restaurant is so cozy and nice. Went here for my boyfriends birthday. You can choose your own wine then drink it at your table! I thought that was pretty cool. Food was good. Service was really good. Our waiter was super nice and informative about the wine they had

[Lola's] I adore Lola's!!! I've never been disappointed here. Great place to take friends, family & I LOVE that even though they have a liquor license now they'll still let you bring your own for a minimal corkage fee. Even waiting outside for a table is part of the experience! Get some wine, kick back or walk to mystery park. Enjoy!

[Cafe Degas] Recommended to me by a friend from Buckhead GA (RIP Tom) that said it suited my personality.  After eating there I took it as an compliment.  A relaxed, eclectic atmosphere situated inside a house with an enclosed air conditioned deck that serves as an extra dining area.

They serve your basic rustic French menu but separate themselves from other French restaurants by excelling in the preparation and presentation of the classics and the daily specials with out the pomp and circumstances.... in short: No Formal Wear Required - BUT you can consider this a strong contender for a special evening or date night, and that's a nice combination for a guy who's looking to impress his date without having to dress.

[French Truck Coffee] Met a group for a meeting here this morning. The decor has a light and bright, happy colored warehousy vibe: simple, clean and happy. Had the NOLA iced: cold brew with milk and a touch of sugar. I care was taken in the making g and it was a fine cup of iced Joe. This place is worth going out of your way to try.

question: bachelorette dinner, upscale vibes, good for large groups
answer: GW Fins is a top choice for a bachelorette dinner with an upscale vibe and great for large groups. The restaurant offers personalized touches like a special menu and confetti, and the service is highly attentive. The food, especially the lobster dumplings and scalibut, is outstanding. Commander's Palace is another excellent option, with a grand atmosphere and excellent service, making it perfect for a celebration. The food is diverse and unique, with standout dishes like the five-hour egg and the Louisiana oyster fondue. For a more mid-range option, Tableau is a great choice, especially for a bachelorette party. The service is welcoming, and the food, like the Redfish Bienville and chicken tableau, is delicious.
contexts:
[GW Fins] We made reservations in advance in honor of our bachelorette.   Upon arrival, our table had flowers and confetti, with a personalized menu congratulating her (along with complementary dessert later). 
The service was terrific and highly attentive.  We enjoyed our meals and fantastic drinks.
 I loved the scallops with mushroom risotto.  Absolutely decadent!
GW Fins was the perfect restaurant to celebrate our big occasion! I highly recommend it

[GW Fins] Let me just start off by saying that I'm a vegetarian, so for me to be giving a seafood place five stars is a big deal. I planned my best friend's bachelorette dinner here a few nights ago and everything about it was perfect. All of my interactions with the staff, even starting with the phone call to confirm the reservation, were really friendly. They gave us a table for ten right in the middle of the room, and they had confetti and a special menu printed up with the bride-to-be's name on the table waiting for us with zero prompting from me. The manager stopped by to say hello and make sure we were all having fun. Our waiter, Troy, charmed everyone's socks off before he could even tell us about the specials. And the food -- literally everyone cleaned their plates. My friends are still talking about the lobster dumplings and scallibut. Even my vegetarian gnocchi was incredible, and even the vegan plate they whipped up for my friend had the carnivores in our party drooling and asking to try her fried leeks. The mashed sweet potatoes with bourbon, vanilla, and banana were probably the most delicious food I tried in New Orleans. The salty malty ice cream pie was killer. Basically this was 100% the perfect spot for a celebration: great food, great atmosphere, great people. And even though it was a great spot for a party, it's definitely not rowdy or noisy. It's the perfect mix of fun and upscale.

[GW Fins] My best girl friends took me here for our fancy dinner night out during my bachelorette last summer, and it was a classy affair of delicious food and drinks, accompanied with fantastic service. 

Must order/try:
* LOBSTER DUMPLINGS
* SCALIBUT

After so many months, I am still gushing about this memorable meal. The lobster dumplings were meaty with the most delicate wonton skin where each bite just melted in my mouth. The scalibut blew our minds away with its perfectly seared scallop crust over a normally mild white fish. It was served with creamy LOBSTER risotto that paired so very well with the fish. The girls and I are from Boston --home of some pretty damn good lobster dishes-- but now I'm starting to think otherwise...

My husband also had his bachelor party in NOLA in the fall, and being good boys, they took our recommendation and had an equally excellent dinner at GW Fins.

+1 star for a personalized keepsake menu and glitter confetti on our table to make us feel extra special :)

[Commander's Palace] This restaurant is the perfect spot for events and nice dinners. There are actually two parts of the restaurant (the front and the back) and an outdoor courtyard in the middle. We came here with a party of 7 celebrating a bachelorette and it definitely was the perfect place for our party.

One of the most exemplary points of our dinner was the service. Everything was served at the same time, and the servers were trained extremely well. Even the host was very gracious, and that experience continued throughout until the end. The food and drinks came at a great time, and the server was there when we needed her. The garlic bread was an amazing start to our meal, the bread was warm and crisp and we finished it in minutes. 

We started out with a few appetizers including the five hour egg, mardi foie, and the louisiana oyster fondue. Wow. All of these dishes were very unique, and it's safe to say i've never had anything like these appetizers before.

The Five Hour Egg- a gently coddled egg on roasted mississippi shiitake mushrooms, crisp potato, brown butter vinaigrette and spiced truffle ($13.50)- the egg with the crispy mushrooms and potato on bottom made an amazing combination. Delicious taste and texture. 

Louisiana Oyster Fondue- crispy oysters and brie caulifower fondue with grilled kale, tomatoes, bacon, parmesan, ciabatta ($12.50)- This was very unique as the flavor of the fondue was more on the cajun side. The fondue was very thick, and with the crispy oysters combined, it was my favorite appetizer. 

Mardi Foie- Foie Gras with foie gras cream cheese stuffed beignets, foie gras royal icing, mardi gras sugar and root beer foie gras ice cream float ($18)- So much foie gras! It was a piece of foie gras and a piece of sweet beignet. Did not expect the two to go so well! Especially after eating all of these beignets everywhere... the root beer float also added an interesting flavor, but overall, a great and unique dish. 

We also got the Soups 1-1-1 ($9.50). which included a sampler of the gumbo, turtle, and soup du jour. The gumbo at Louisiana is not what we usually get in California, so it was really interesting to try. The turtle soup was great! I did not expect to like it so much, and it was very unique. I did not remember what the last soup was, but it was a creamy soup of some kind. All three were great though .Would definitely recommend this if you want to try their variety of soups.

For the entrees, all of us got the french white truffle and winter mushroom risotto ($26) with lobster (+$12). The risotto was very creamy and was cooked to perfection, and the lobster really added a nice touch to the risotto. Love how they utilize their truffle here! Too bad this dish was heavy.. we could not finish our food.

For dessert, we got both the souffle and the strawberry shortcake. We thought both were good, but nothing special. Both are made on the spot. 

Overall, a great dinner and fine dining experience at Commander's Palace. I could see why it's on the to go to lists on many blogs!

[Commander's Palace] I came here with a group of friends for a bachelorette party dinner. The restaurant is huge with many rooms and perfect for big groups. The interior had a nice old charm to it, characteristic of New Orleans as a city. There were balloons at tables that were celebrating birthdays, which was a nice touch. We were impressed by how one of the staff members was so attentive in the beginning to change our napkins from white to black when she saw that we were wearing black dresses. However, our waiter was not very friendly throughout our meal. Most of our party ordered from Chef Tory's Three Course Offerings. The gumbo and turtle soups were okay but not particularly impressive. For entrees, my friend and I shared the Wagyu beef, which wasn't as marbled as we would have liked, but still tender with delicious mashed potatoes as an accompaniment. We also ordered the crispy soft shell crab, which was crispy as advertised with a nice flavor. We were very excited to try the Creole bread pudding souffle as we had heard rave reviews from a friend - "I dream about that soufflé" were her exact words, so who wouldn't have high expectations?! While it was a good dessert, we didn't feel that it was spectacular, and the whiskey cream sauce was too strong for our taste. I really liked the chewy top of the soufflé though! I'm not a fan of cooked fruit, but actually felt that the roasted apple and caramel cobbler was better. Overall, we had a pleasant dining experience and feel that the food and prices, with the ambience, make this restaurant a good option for nice meals or celebrations.

[Commander's Palace] We came in to celebrate and birthday and a bachelorette at the same time. Luckily for us, we met one of the owners Dollie. She was having dinner next to our table of 12 girls and she came over to say hi, bought us all a round of champagne. That is southern hospitality that I can say I have never experienced any where else. The level of service was supreme. I've eaten and fancy places in NY and never had my meals served like this before. I loved it because the ambiance was perfect. We stayed past closing (oops) and took lots of pics. They also wrapped up the food in cute little aluminum trinkets that they got creative with.

The food prices were affordable for a 5 star restaruant. I think most people had appetizers to share with an entree which was more than enough. Almost everyone had a little packup aluminum trinket. I had the vegetarian mushroom risotto which was on the salty side, also the word used to describe most entrees. The app that everyone loved was the one with pork belly and fried oyster. I could have ordered that all night if I knew how good it was! They also sent me some balloons to decorate the table which was really cute and a sweet touch. And then brought out a praline sundae for my with Congrats on the plate. I've never really felt so honored at a dinner before so that was one amazing experience. I would definitely come back here for the hospitality and service. Everything came out at the same time, all 12 of our dishes at once.

[Tableau] Went here for a bachelorette party dinner a group of 10. They seated us at beautiful square on the second floor right by a smaller bar. The table was a great option to easily see everyone and have a conversation without having to yell at the table. Staff was welcoming and attentive. They even turned off the ac near us when they saw us shivering. For entrees several of the girls got the Redfish Bienville and raved about it the rest of the weekend. My sister had the steak frites medium and rated that a 3/5 flavor was bland. I had the chicken tableau. The chicken was fall off the bone and a great portion size. For dessert they treated us with the Creme brûlée which was also fantastic. It is a little spendy and would recommend more for a birthday or anniversary setting over a bachelorette party

[Tableau] One of my favorite restaurants in the entire city. From food, service, to atmosphere, this checks it all for me. Ate dinner here for a bachelorette party and they were incredibly accommodating to all 14 of us and did an amazing job making the bride feel celebrated. Really yummy craft cocktails and great plates to share. 

Have the most fun second floor balcony! Hosted a birthday brunch in the green room upstairs, and it was so memorable. The buffet style brunch was fresh and flavorful. I could've bathed in the barbecue shrimp and grits. The jazz band is fantastic, always playing crowd favorites! :)

[Tableau] We had a wonderful time at Tableau while in New Orleans celebrating our friend's bachelorette party. We were a party of 8 *slightly rowdy* females. The staff were amazing and treated us with such kindness and respect. You don't always find that when serving a large party. Our food was delicious and came out timely and hot. Katie Hutchinson, the manager, made sure to stop by and congratulate my friend on her engagement and offered to get the table anything we might need. I would absolutely recommend this restaurant to anyone  and will definitely be back when we visit New Orleans again.

[Brennan's] Wow-what can I say?  Honestly, this was the best meal I've had all summer! (and I haven't exactly been dieting...)
Came here for my bachelorette party/dinner with some great friends and we were all very impressed and happy with our choice to come here!
I guess I should start with the service-It was wonderful.  We felt so welcomed and relaxed : ) 
Anecdote to help you understand: I accidentally dropped my knife at one point and it hit my dress leaving a small but noticeable stain (at my own bachelorette party! I'm not super high maintenance or anything but any girl would frown at such a faux pas). The waiter immediately got me a fresh knife and a napkin along with a glass of seltzer so I could remove the stain...came right out! My hero ! 
Back to business, we ordered some cocktails to start and then a sommelier introduced himself to help us pick out some wine.  We ordered 3 apps for the table: roasted oysters, octopus and lobster.  All three were great but my favorite was the lobster.  I'm usually not big on seafood and this is only the second time or so I've had lobster because I've just never been a fan but the flavors and textures in all these dishes were seriously bomb.  
Moving on to the main dish, I had the steak dianne (pretty sure it was a special that night) and everything from presentation to the last bite was so good. The steak was juicy and flavorful yet not overly heavy and it came with some vegg and potatoes. Classic American dish done so right and they cooked it at the table so we got a little show (according to my fiancee, this was the only all male show we saw that night : )
Dessert was a bananas foster (because these guys literally invented it!) which was prepared table side as well along with complimentary creme brulee and sugar cookies-family style desserts are the best way to end such a meal and even though we were full we persevered...it was all sugary goodness-decadent but not too heavy.
We stayed here ruminating for something like 4 hours...it really felt like we were at a table at a friend's house (a very wealthy friend with a very nice/big house, but still). I would come back for dinner and special occasions. I also hear brunch here is not to be missed.  
I will remember this meal and time with my friends very fondly for a long time to come!

ps not to be tacky but I have to mention that all this for 7 people was around 500 before tip...in my stomping grounds of NYC this would have been double that easily!

[Brennan's] Came here for a bachelorette party brunch and it was fantastic! If you are wanting some instagram-worthy photos, this is the place! Located right in the French Quarter and steps from our hotel, it was very easy to find. You can't miss an iconic bright pink building. We made reservations for a party of 8 and were quickly seated in the Audubon room - a Parisian styled room with peach pink walls lined with stunning oyster plates and a beautiful patterned tiled floor. This was our favorite room out of all the rooms! 

Now onto the food. It was our first time here and everything on the menu sounded amazing. Our waitress was so sweet and gave us recommendations on what to order or else we would have ordered the entire menu. Drink wise we all ordered a fruity sparkler (I can't remember the name of it). So we started off with the egg yolk carpaccio with grilled shrimp and sweet potato - very good and the presentation was wonderful. We passed on the turtle soup although I wish I had gotten it now. So instead we got the seafood gumbo (shrimp, andouille, oysters) and it was very tasty. Next I ordered eggs Owen (red wine braised short rib, potatoes, poached eggs, Hollandaise sauce, and Marchand de vin aka red wine reduction sauce). All the flavors were out of this world, the short rib was one of the best I ever had - so tender and juicy with just the right amount of fat! We didn't have any room for dessert but I will definitely be coming back to try the bananas foster one day.

After we got our check we headed out to the courtyard and it felt as if we were walking into a beautiful lush fairytale. The exposed brick along with the lush greenery and the fountain looked stunning. The staff were also very kind by offering to take a bunch of photos for our bachelorette party! This ended up being my favorite restaurant from our whole trip (we visited about 7).

[Restaurant August] Came here for a fancy bachelorette dinner. Super quaint and quiet place - good for romantic dinners. The service was great and the food was delicious! I would take one star off only because we had made a reservation weeks prior and our table wasn't ready when we got there. And put it back on for their complimentary appetizer and dessert!

[Restaurant August] Absolutely stellar service, elegant and stately decor and incredible food! Gorgeous huge rose floral display in the center of the room, stunning crystal chandeliers.
