The dishes were ALL delicious with so much complexity with the preparation process and various components, sous vide, reductions, concentrated sauces, whipped ricotta, mousse...I couldn't begin to remember every explanation of each plate, but that hardly mattered as each bite of every dish was exquisite. The food experience was further enhanced by the traditional and proper cutlery used for each course as well as the knowledge and effusiveness of our waiter, Captain Robert Kerner. He was a delight and played right into our charade of faux Southern names and gaiety as well as bringing out many special surprises for the birthday lady and gentleman.  The cocktails, wine, dessert were also incredible and Captain Robert's vast knowledge of every dish and wine pairing was nothing short of amazing. August was definitely worth every penny and perfect for a special occasion.

question: wheelchair accessible restaurant that caters events
answer: Empire State Delicatessen is a great choice for event catering, with high praise for their professionalism and delicious food. Fritai also offers excellent catering services, with a 4.5-star rating and positive feedback from customers about the quality of the food and service. Both places are wheelchair accessible and have received positive reviews for their event catering.
contexts: [Empire State Delicatessen] I ordered a Catering for an event and the food was great as well as their professionalism and customer service. I highly recommend Empire State Deli for your event.

[Pizza Delicious] Had a wonderful experience ordering catering for a party of 15 flawlessly delivered to our hotel room for a reasonable fee. From the moment I called, to the day of, there was nothing but kindness and professionalism.  We had a variety of cheese and meat pies, salad, garlic bread, and cookies ordered: everything was soooo good. They make their namesake proud!

[Trenasse] If I could give it 6 stars, I would. Reservations usually aren't needed, but on Yelp it said they allowed pets, so I made a reservation through OpenTable and noted that we have a small dog. I received a call from the host who informed me that only applied to service animals, but she offered to set up seating on the patio for us and the dog. The patio had an awning and it rained hard but was still in the 70s. We had the gumbo, the blue crab bisque, a shrimp entree and mahi mahi. For dessert it was beignets and peach cobbler. Everything was spectacular. Our server was the most attentive server I have ever had...which is especially great when you're the only party on the patio and servers sometimes forget about them. Ours was Johnny on the spot. We were on a long trip across the country and had been doing a fair bit of fast food and takeout, so it was nice to have a great dining experience.

[Fritai ] Ordered Fritai for a medium sized catering event and was so happy with the service and quality of food.  Charly was a pleasure to work with.  Definitely recommend it next time you need a caterer!

[Li'l Dizzy's Cafe] Great food, attentive service. Customers are a mix of locals and tourists, and the non-locals are welcomed without comment. We had the Sunday brunch buffet, and it was well worth it - the fried chicken, gumbo, French toast, and bread pudding were absolutely delicious.

[Li'l Dizzy's Cafe] Best breakfast buffet, crab & shrimp omlets, fried chicken, gumbo, great french toast with bananas and strawberries. Large ice tea and all for $20. Alittle bit of everything.  It is small and crowded so make reservations,  especially on Sunday for brunch buffet. Parking is on street in Treme.

question: dressy dinner spot with live music
answer: For a dressy dinner spot with live music, Arnaud's French 75 Bar is a standout. The place feels like stepping back in time to the 1930s, with its elegant decor and classic cocktails. While it's a bit dressy, the atmosphere is welcoming and the live music adds to the experience. Another great option is Foundation Room, which offers a unique and intimate setting with live jazz, featuring a cozy lounge and an Art Deco corridor. The eclectic decor and live music make it a quintessential New Orleans cocktail bar experience.
contexts: [Arnaud's French 75 Bar] Elegant but not stuffy is the best description of this gem, connected to the excellent Arnaud's Restaurant. Staff is very professional , impeccably dressed and friendly making excellent cocktails, and serving bar foods off the restaurant menu, they will answer any question regarding cocktails and food and with make recommendations according to your likes. Sunday evening is my usual time because not as crowded but anytime is good. It's almost like stepping into another time because with the old tile floor, beautiful beveled mirrors and windows, funny monkey lamps and the old French "café" music it's as if you back in 1920 Paris in fact you almost expect to see Hemingway in the corner eating raw oysters and drinking Pastis. The only thing that makes the elegance not "quite deliver" is the dress of the customers.

[Arnaud's French 75 Bar] My husband and I are just shy of 30 but we are true old souls at heart. We walked right past the crazy drunkards on Bourbon Street and walked into French75 feeling like we stepped back in time to the 1930's. Of course, we were the youngest people in there, but it was definitely more our speed than chugging beer in the middle of the street.

French75 is a classy bar with classic/vintage cocktails and a cigar bar. We didn't smoke cigars this evening but I think I'd like to go back for one before we head out of town. The bartender and the waiter were very knowledgeable about the drinks and their components and were super friendly. 

The drinks were delicious and if you're a scotch/whiskey/bourbon drinker, you will love this place.

The space itself is made up of elegant arm chairs and settees with dim lights - very romantic, but at the same time it's manly enough for drinks and cigars with just the guys.

[Arnaud's French 75 Bar] Classy. Sophisticated. Timeless. Intimate. If you want to feel like you just walked onto the set of the movie Midnight in Paris, go to Arnaud's French 75.

Everything about this bar was perfect. I'm really into cocktails and try to see lots of bars on my vacations, and this was quite possibly the nicest bar I have ever had the pleasure of visiting. My boyfriend and I came in shortly past 11pm on a weekday and there were only a couple of other people inside. We were seated at a small table and while we tried to decide which drinks to get, I admired the classic tile floors and eccentric monkey lamps. A young man in a tuxedo served us water. We settled on a French 75 and a Sazerac and they did not disappoint- stiff and made with premium spirits. 

All the proportions and textures of the interior were so pleasing- from the impressive, intricately carved wood counter, to the the height of the ceiling and the mirror on the back wall. It just felt really good to sit there and take it all in. Adding to the ambiance was the heady aroma of cigar smoke. Usually I really don't like the smell of cigars, but there, it just fit.

The French 75 Bar is a special, special place!

[Chophouse New Orleans] The best surprise in the Big Easy. First off, this resturant was reccommended by the Conceirge at the Ritz Carlton New Orleans. Little did we know we be in to a most memorable dining experience that tops the ranks of most fine dinning in this busy city full of great food. And it tops the top of the list in New Orleans. First, upon entering the venue from walking distance from the hotel, we almost missed it, as it wasn't shiny glamoring with exotic neon lights. The sign well lit located about 3-4 blocks from busy 'ol' Burboun street and Canal. The front has valet parking if needed, since it's located in downtown area. Could be difficult to find parking as in any downtown setting. Upon entry our party of three was greeted by a nice lady host. Didn't get her name. We were seated immediately on a Sunday night at 8pm Jan 29th, 2012. At first glance you notice a nice arrangement of round and square tableclothed tables in a nice and elegant basemen/cellar almost train station feeling with no dirty train. Don't get me wrong, it was nice and cozy feeling. There was a separate room for the bar area and a really delightful live entertainer "folk/pop/rock" genre music. The singer/songwriter who entertained us was Amanda Walker. Very entertaining and great music that brings liveliness to the place. Plays the piano like a champ and sings with aces. Very nice I might add. Especially on what I consider a late Sunday night dinner at 8pm. Our server who is Jeanne, the night manager, she was terrific. More on that later. Upon being seated, we were given the usual meet and greet given a wine list and menu. After a few minutes of trying to decide, we asked Jeanne what she recommended to satisfy our Red-wine-acholic selves. Mind you were are opting for the steak at this resturant as our meal of choice. After a few rounds of I want this, I want that, our server Jeanne recommended a Sonoma-Cutrer Pinot Noir 2007. The wine selection was firm, intense and vibrant yet not too fruity or chalky. It put us in the right mood for a three guy party. Mind you we've been working most of the day and tired yet ready for a nice dinner, with preconceived notion of quick bite and get to sleep. Needless to say we stayed well past closing time.
Onto the food: first off for an appetizer we ordered the Florida Stone Crab and the Carpaccio Prime beef tenderloin. The stone crab was nice thick and juicy. I cannot comment because I'm allergic, but my companions throughly enjoyed the stone crab. The Carpaccio was awesome. The cut was oval and the size of the plate itself, laid perfectly flat topped with decorative spinach and cheese. The meat was melt in your mouth buttery smooth and cut thin as a credit card. Talk about perfection! Fantastic choice!  Our server, Jeanne suggested a crack of pepper which enhanced the appetizing flavors. Next onto the the entree. This place serves only USDA grade prime beef cuts, aged inhouse. I skipped salad, but the others said it was good. Not going into salad details on this post.  We opted for Filet Mignon 8oz and the New York Strip 10oz. Filet Mignon cooked at med-rear and Strip at Med-well. But first, the sides. We had a side of Steamed Asparagus and Lyonnaise. The Lyonnaise is bite sized cube cut potatoes fried with garlic powder and diced onions. Reminds me of grandmas good old southern cooking and that means a lot when you can eat it and say ohhhh ohhh.  The asparagus.. was good too. Now the meat. The filet mignon came out delicious. You know a good steak when the meat is red med rear in the middle with no blood juices flowing. The meat on the outside seared to perfection and meat in the middle melting as you down it with the wine. YUM.. This was the case for both the Filet Mignon. The NY Strip was cooked medium well and came out fantastic also. The meat was cooked to perfection with a rear-pink middle. Mind you NY Strip meat is tougher than Filet Mignon but this one came out like a champ. Not tough at all. The juices ran with no sign of blood and middle coming out pink for perfection. Our server took the time to acquaint herself with the three of us and gladly gave us the details of how the resturant came to be the history, how they selected location and the history of the building and surronding. She made a suggestion to try to Key Lime Pie. All I can say is sweet. The keylime pie came in its real color - yellowish and tasted superb. None of the fake food coloring green. This keylime pie you would have to eat from crust to finish as it was that good. The crust had a little ginger taste but works well with a grainy crust and the natural keylime flavor was smooth. All I can say is that with all the food selections in this city, this is one that you must try. Save the wait at other high dollar venues and get into this one.

[Chophouse New Orleans] Home run! Best meal, ambiance and experience maybe ever for me, my wife, plus one. Cocktails at the bar probably enhanced our experience. The piano player set a relaxing tone. Reserved table was on time. Food quality was the highlight. Fairly pricey.

[Chophouse New Orleans] An excellent dinner complemented by very good service.  We had salads to start, one Caesar and one chopped.  Pretty ordinary.  A very tasty strip steak cooked black and blue, as ordered.  The ladies shared a filet and liked it very much.  Side of onion rings and French fries was also, like the salads, nothing special.  The desert, a chocolate cake ala mode was extraordinary.  Rich, moist with chocolate chips in the frosting, and large enough to serve four.

[Foundation Room] The ambiance of this place is like nothing I've seen before. They had a cozy lounge with chesterfield sofas, a full bar serving prohibition-era cocktails, and a live jazz trio. You enter the Foundation Room through a highly stylized Art Deco corridor and elevator, proceeded by a stained glass corridor. The walls are upholstered with Indian blankets embroidered with tiny mirrors and the carpeting is made of Persian rugs tacked together. The dining area features a domed ceiling and a wall of temperature controlled wine. The host staff made the experience feel very mysterious and exclusive, inviting us to the lounge and serving us champagne while we waited for our table. The waitress and kitchen accommodated my dietary restrictions (pescatarian, dairy-free). The tuna tartare appetizer special was tasty, and the salad was fine. The lettuces were very nice but I held the cheese so it wasn't anything too special. My fish and veggie entree was tasty and was made special for me to meet my dietary needs. The cocktails were also tasty - I did the Cider cocktail and a French 75. After dinner we hung out in the uncrowded lounge and enjoyed some more tasty libations while listening to the jazz trio. Quintessential New Orleans cocktail bar experience.

[Foundation Room] Normally, I would find myself on the other side of the velvet ropes at places like this, but a friend "put me on the list" to see her girlfriend's jazzy lounge band, Soulkestra, play a few sets.  So I have visited the Foundation Room three times, and surprisingly I was able to set aside the anti-elitist hang-ups that accompany my low birth and actually enjoy myself there.  

In fact, it was not until my third visit that I learned during a conversation with one of the paying members that this was actually a private venue.  I just assumed it was HOB's attempt at an "intimate jazz venue."  While I would not pay money to purposefully seclude myself in a private bar, as my life is thankfully devoid of paparrazi and hangers-on, I can certainly see the appeal.  The barmen are pros, the drinks are properly stiff, and there is a stairway leading to a private-access balcony overlooking the HOB main stage.  

The lounge's decor is wall-to-wall neo-opium den chic, complete with a replica "Reclining Buddha" statue on the hearth of the artificial fire.  There are plush couches and lounge chairs and even a bottle-service area that I assume is an anti-malarial quarantine because its semicircular booth is partitioned with mosquito netting.  Most impressive to me, however, was the carpeting, which a manager explained to me was actually not carpeting per se but dozens and dozens of Persian rugs stitched together to cover the entire lounge.

There is typically a pretty constant stream of mini-skirted "woo girls" and the untucked-oxford shirted men that tend to surround them.  If that's your thing, well go get em, tiger, but you'll have to plunk down the coin.  As for me, I'll just enjoy a couple gin drinks and some good music in this cool, relaxing lounge.  3.5 rounded up.

[Foundation Room] Outstanding atmosphere.  Small quiet dining room right outside a very classy but eclectically decorated live music bar to enjoy before dinner.  

Great food and service.
